source.title: Conjunctive reward-place coding properties of dorsal distal CA1 hippocampus cells.

confidence_rationale: Speaks to the architectural question underneath SD-024 -- whether reward information enters the spatial map at all, and in what form -- and answers yes, but as a continuum from pure place cells through hybrid cells to dedicated reward cells, with reward cells responding to reward DELIVERY rather than expectation. Moderate confidence: it is a reanalysis of existing recordings in a modest venue, and the coding scheme it finds is a third option that neither SD-024 nor its main competitor predicts.
failure_signatures: Reward cells responded mostly to reward DELIVERY rather than to its expectation, which cuts against SD-024's scaling of the allocation signal by drive_level (an expectation-side quantity) and sits in tension with Krishnan et al. 2022's expectation-dependent ramping signal. The literature is not internally settled on whether the allocating signal is expectation-driven or delivery-driven.

A subpopulation transitioned between place-cell and reward-cell properties within a single 5-task session, so the mapping between 'unit' and 'what it represents' is not stable on the timescale REE's FIFO center lifecycle assumes.
Some cells were typical place cells wholly insensitive to reward location -- reward influence is heterogeneous across the population, not a uniform field-wide modulation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Reanalysis of CA1 recordings across five consecutive tasks with manipulated reward locations and spatial context reveals a continuum of coding properties: typical place cells insensitive to reward, dedicated reward cells firing at correct rewarded feeders regardless of context, and hybrid cells responding to both. Some cells transition between these regimes within a session. The authors argue spatial and value representations are not independent.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the general architectural move SD-024 makes -- putting reward-conditioned structure inside the hippocampal representation rather than only downstream -- and thereby softens Duvelle et al. 2019's value-free-map conclusion. But it locates that structure in a DEDICATED SUBPOPULATION with distinct tuning, not in locally denser sampling of the same spatial code. That is a third architecture, and REE currently implements neither it nor a clean version of the gain alternative.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Reanalysis of a previously published dataset (Gauthier & Tank recordings), not a fresh experiment, and dorsal DISTAL CA1 specifically -- a subregion with known distinctive reward and object sensitivity, so the finding may not generalise to CA1 as a whole, let alone to a generic hippocampal residue field. The cell-type continuum has no counterpart in REE's RBF field, where all centers are homogeneous, so the translation is loose by construction.
mapping.source_context: Rats (Brown Norway), five consecutive tasks manipulating reward location and spatial context; reanalysis of dorsal distal CA1 tetrode recordings.

confidence_components.notes: Reanalysis rather than primary experiment, modest venue, single subregion -- source quality capped at 0.6. Mapping fidelity is the weak term: a heterogeneous cell-type continuum does not map cleanly onto a homogeneous RBF field. Included because it is the clearest statement that the delivery-vs-expectation question is open, which bears directly on SD-024's dopamine_signal formula.
